```{r Data download, include=FALSE}
if (!file.exists("./pci_data.csv")) {
  stop("NCR dataset not found! Please check that you have a single CSV file named \"pci_data.csv\" in the current directory!",
       call. = FALSE)
}

#Load in the helper functions/data required
source("HelperFunctions.R")

#Read in data from PowerBI
pci_data_raw <- readr::read_csv("./pci_data.csv")
# pci_data <- readr::read_csv("./pci_data.csv", col_types = colTypes)
```

```{r Report context setup, include=FALSE}
target_po <- params$target_po
period_start <- params$period_start
period_end <- params$period_end
```

```{r Data transformation, include=FALSE}
pci_data <- prepare_pci_data(pci_data_raw) |>
  # Format the Procedure Operator Name
  dplyr::mutate(
    po_name = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(po, ","),
      paste0(
        stringr::str_split_i(trimws(po), ", ", 2),
        " ",
        stringr::str_split_i(trimws(po), ", ", 1)
      ),
      trimws(po)
    )|> 
      stringr::str_to_title() |>
      stringr::str_remove("Dr ")
  ) |>
  # Create Count column for Number of PCIs
  dplyr::mutate(
    count_pci = 1
  ) |>
  # Add comparison_group based on selected targeted clinician
  dplyr::mutate(
    comparison_group = factor(
      dplyr::if_else(po == target_po, "Target Clinician", "Other Clinicians"),
      levels = c("Target Clinician", "Other Clinicians")
    )
  ) |>
  # Multiple los columns for mean and median
  dplyr::mutate(
    los_mean = los,
    los_median = los
  ) |>
  # Filter for period start and period end for this report
  dplyr::filter(
    dop >= params$period_start & dop <= params$period_end
  )

if (params$period_frequency == "quarterly") {
  pci_data <- pci_data |>
  # Change period_end to be quarterly instead
  dplyr::mutate(
    period_end = lubridate::quarter(period_end, type = "date_last")
  )
}
```

# Patient Demographics

## Patient Characteristics by Clinical Presentation

```{r demographics_by_acs_table, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
demographic_tbl_summary <- function(data) {
  data |>
    gtsummary::tbl_summary(
      include = c(age, severe_obesity, ppci, pcabg, db, pvd, los_mean, los_median, los_cat),
      by = "comparison_group",
      label = list(
        age ~ "Age",
        severe_obesity ~ "Severe Obesity (BMI ≥ 35 kg/m²)",
        ppci ~ "Previous PCI",
        pcabg ~ "Previous CABG",
        db ~ "Diabetic",
        pvd ~ "Peripheral Vascular Disease",
        los_mean ~ "Average Length of Stay (Mean)",
        los_median ~ "Average Length of Stay (Median)",
        los_cat ~ "Length of Stay"
      ),
      statistic = list(
        c(age, los_mean) ~ "{mean}",
        c(los_median) ~ "{median}",
        c(severe_obesity, ppci, pcabg, db, pvd, los_cat) ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
      ),
      digits = list(
        c(age) ~ 1,
        c(los_mean) ~ 1,
        c(los_median) ~ 0
      ),
      missing = "no"
    )
}

tbl_stratified_and_overall <- function(data, func_tbl_summary, label_name = "Characteristic") {
  # Create a stratified table by ACS category
  tbl_stratified <- data |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      acs_cat_factor = factor(acs_cat, levels = c("STEMI", "NSTEMI", "Non-ACS"), ordered = TRUE)
    ) |>
    gtsummary::tbl_strata(
      strata = "acs_cat_factor",
      .tbl_fun = 
        ~ .x |>
        func_tbl_summary()
    )
  
  # Create an overall table for all PCIs
  tbl_overall <- data |>
    func_tbl_summary() |> 
    gtsummary::modify_spanning_header(gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~ "**All PCIs**")
  
  # Merge the stratified and overall tables
  tbl_final <- list(tbl_stratified, tbl_overall) |>
    gtsummary::tbl_merge(tab_spanner = FALSE) |>
    # Change label name for first column
    gtsummary::modify_header(label ~ paste0("**", label_name, "**")) |>
    # Force the header to split into two lines with the N = {n} on the second line
    gtsummary::modify_header(gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}**          N = {n}") |>
    # Convert to gt object
    gtsummary::as_gt() |>
    # Put a border on the left of the stat columns and italicise the stat columns
    gt::tab_style(
      style = gt::cell_borders(sides = "left", color = "black"),
      locations = list(
        gt::cells_column_labels(columns = stat_1_2),
        gt::cells_body(columns = stat_1_2),
        gt::cells_column_spanners(spanners = "**All PCIs**")
      )
    ) |>
    gt::tab_style(
      style = gt::cell_text(style = "italic"),
      locations = list(
        gt::cells_body(columns = c(stat_1_2, stat_2_2))
      )
    )
  
  return(tbl_final)
}

tbl_stratified_and_overall(pci_data |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(age) & !is.na(inds_cat) & !is.na(acs_cat)), demographic_tbl_summary)

```

```{r demographic_by_acs_plots, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#| fig-format: svg
#| fig-width: 10.4
#| fig-height: 2
#| out-width: "100%"

stat_ggplot2 <- function(data, stat, title, x_axis_short_label) {
  # Calculate Required Statistics for ggplot visual
  stat_data <- rbind(
    data |>
      dplyr::group_by(comparison_group, acs_cat) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        stat = {{stat}}
      ),
    data |>
      dplyr::group_by(comparison_group) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        stat = {{stat}}
      ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        acs_cat = "All"
      )
  ) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = comparison_group,
      values_from = stat
    ) |>
    dplyr::rename(
      stat_target = `Target Clinician`,
      stat_other = `Other Clinicians`
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      acs_cat = factor(acs_cat, levels = c("Non-ACS", "NSTEMI", "STEMI", "All"))
    )
  
  # Initialise ggplot chart
  min_point <- min(c(stat_data$stat_target, stat_data$stat_other), na.rm = TRUE)
  max_point <- max(c(stat_data$stat_target, stat_data$stat_other), na.rm = TRUE)
  ggplot2_output <- ggplot2::ggplot(stat_data) +
    # Add horizontal bars for Target Clinician
    ggplot2::geom_bar(
      ggplot2::aes(
        y = acs_cat,
        x = stat_target
      ),
      stat = "identity",
      fill = "#1f77b4"
    ) +
    # Add points for Other Clinician average
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      ggplot2::aes(
        y = acs_cat,
        x = stat_other,
        color = "Other Clinicians"
      ),
      size = 4,
      color = "#7B1500"
    ) +
    # Add y axis label
    ggplot2::ylab("PCI Indication") +
    # Add x axis label
    ggplot2::xlab(x_axis_short_label) +
    # Set x-axis limits
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(min_point * 0.9, max_point * 1.1)
    ) +
    # Add title
    ggplot2::ggtitle(title) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, size = 16,
                                         face = "bold", family = "sans",
                                         margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 0)),
      # panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      # panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, color = "#000000"),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10, color = "#000000")
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
    
  return(ggplot2_output)
}

# Age
p_age <- stat_ggplot2(
  data = pci_data |> 
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(age) & !is.na(inds_cat) & !is.na(acs_cat)),
  stat = mean(age),
  title = "Average Age (Mean) by Indication",
  x_axis_short_label = "Average Age (Mean)"
)

# Previous PCI
p_ppci <- stat_ggplot2(
  data = pci_data |> 
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(age) & !is.na(inds_cat) & !is.na(acs_cat)),
  stat = sum(ppci)/sum(count_pci) * 100,
  title = "Previous PCI (%) by Indication",
  x_axis_short_label = "Previous PCI (%)"
)

# Previous CABG
p_pcabg <- stat_ggplot2(
  data = pci_data |> 
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(age) & !is.na(inds_cat) & !is.na(acs_cat)),
  stat = sum(pcabg)/sum(count_pci) * 100,
  title = "Previous CABG (%) by Indication",
  x_axis_short_label = "Previous CABG (%)"
)

# Diabetic
p_db <- stat_ggplot2(
  data = pci_data |> 
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(age) & !is.na(inds_cat) & !is.na(acs_cat)),
  stat = sum(db)/sum(count_pci) * 100,
  title = "Diabetic (%) by Indication",
  x_axis_short_label = "Diabetic (%)"
)

# PVD
p_pvd <- stat_ggplot2(
  data = pci_data |> 
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(age) & !is.na(inds_cat) & !is.na(acs_cat)),
  stat = sum(pvd)/sum(count_pci) * 100,
  title = "PVD (%) by Indication",
  x_axis_short_label = "PVD (%)"
)

# Average Length of Stay (Mean)
p_los <- stat_ggplot2(
  data = pci_data |> 
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(age) & !is.na(inds_cat) & !is.na(acs_cat)),
  stat = mean(los_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
  title = "Average LoS (Mean) by Indication",
  x_axis_short_label = "Average LoS (Mean)"
)

# Render plots using patchwork
p_age | p_los
p_ppci | p_pcabg
p_db | p_pvd
```

# Appendix

## Definitions

### 30-Day Stroke
Description: Proportion of patients that undergo a PCI procedure that had a new stroke during the 30-day follow-up period.

Denominator: Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure.

Numerator: Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure and were admitted into hospital for Stroke within 30 days of discharge from hospital. The stroke admission can be either to the emergency department or to an inpatient bed.

### 30-Day Cardiac Rehospitalisation
Description: Proportion of patients that undergo a PCI procedure that had cardiac hospitalisation within 30 days.

Denominator: Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure.

Numerator: Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure and had a cardiac rehospitalisation within 30 days of discharge, where a cardiac rehospitalisation is defined as an in-patient admission that includes, but is not limited to any of the following circumstances: heart failure; acute coronary syndrome (e.g. STEMI, NSTEMI; recurrent or unstable angina); arrhythmia; elective (non emergency) PCI or CABG etc.


### 30-Day Mortality After PCI
Description: Proportion of patients that undergo a PCI procedure that died in-hospital or within 30 days of discharge.  

Denominator: Number of patients that undergo a PCI procedure.

Numerator: Number of procedures that undergo a PCI procedure with a discharge status of death or death within 30 days of discharge.

## Interpreting Patterns in SPC Charts and Funnel Plots

The following patterns are highlighted in this report.

### Funnel Plot Outlier

An identified point that exceeds 3 sigma limits from the mean.

```{r showing Funnel Outlier sample, echo = FALSE}
funnel_example_plotly(fpl_example_data)
```

### Astronomical Point

An identified point that exceeds 3 sigma limits from the mean.

```{r showing astro sample, echo = FALSE}
spc_example_plotly(spc_example_data_astro)
```

### Trend

Five or more consecutively increasing or decreasing points.

```{r showing trend sample, echo = FALSE}
spc_example_plotly(spc_example_data_trend)
```

### Two in Three

Two out of Three consecutive points exceeding 2 sigma limits from the mean.

```{r showing two in three sample, echo = FALSE}
spc_example_plotly(spc_example_data_twothree)
```

### Shift

Seven or more consecutive points above or below the mean.

```{r showing shift sample, echo = FALSE}
spc_example_plotly(spc_example_data_shift)
```
